> An interactive digital hourglass and physics-based tilt toy powered by an ESP32. It uses a MAX7219 8x8 LED matrix display and a GY-521 (MPU-6050) motion sensor to simulate real-time falling sand particles responding to gravity and shaking gestures.

### What was done:
Configured and aligned the component layout in the KiCad PCB editor for Gravity-Matrix. Set the exact 25.4 mm (1.0") center-to-center pitch for the two 19-pin ESP32 socket headers (J1 and J2) to ensure precise mechanical clearance. Reoriented the 1.3" ST7789 IPS display header (J3) inward, repositioned the MPU-6050 sensor (J5) away from the controller outline, and placed 100nF decoupling capacitors (C1, C2) directly next to the supply pins. Defined the preliminary 80 x 65 mm board perimeter on Edge.Cuts.

![_gravity-matrix_KiCAD — Schaltplaneditor 27.10.2026 11_36_49](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/abd5f57e3ea757f406741252f993043c38fab22690026c17837f68dbdb8ae730.png)

### 2026-11-01: ### What was done:

**4h**

### What was done:
1. **System Architecture & Hardware Abstraction:**
   * Created the central hardware pinout and configuration file (`config.h`) for the ST7789 IPS display via SPI (GPIO 18, 23, 2, 4) and the GY-521 MPU-6050 accelerometer via I2C (GPIO 21, 22).
   * Implemented a lean direct-register I2C sensor driver (`imu.cpp`) to stream raw acceleration vectors continuously without relying on heavy external third-party libraries.

2. **Analog Clock GUI (`clock_view.cpp`):**
   * Engineered an analog watch-face GUI with trigonometric calculation ($sin / cos$) for hour, minute, and second hand angles.
   * Built differential rendering: only the previous coordinates of the hands are redrawn to the background color on each second tick to eliminate full-screen display flicker completely.

3. **Cellular Automata Sand Physics (`sand_view.cpp`):**
   * Programmed a real-time falling sand simulation on a 60x60 grid ($4 \times 4$ pixel scaling) responding directly to physical gravity vectors from the MPU-6050.
   * Added directional quantization and natural angle-of-repose collision handling, allowing sand particles to tumble over piles and settle against chamber boundaries.
   * Optimized screen updates to only draw modified grid cells for high, stable framerates on the 240x240 screen.

4. **Navigation & Main State Machine (`menu_view.cpp` & `main.cpp`):**
   * Created an interactive tilt-controlled menu interface supporting gesture selection (tilting to cycle options, shaking/flicking to launch).
   * Tied the display, IMU, clock view, and sand simulator together inside a clean state machine in `main.cpp` and resolved PlatformIO build/linker issues.
